budget_items.topic: Task 1 - background data collection and review
budget_items.what_was_said: The task force said this task was cut from the Weston and Sampson scope, though there was confusion in the room about which task number this was.
The online web application/tool, done mostly by communities tiered within SFH, was removed from the scope; the underlying GIS delineation of commercial parcels was said to remain.

budget_items.topic: Impervious cover GIS data layer - parcel count and cost
budget_items.what_was_said: The number of parcels to be covered by the impervious-cover GIS layer was discussed with several conflicting figures read off different copies of the proposal; the group settled that around 700 parcels, covering commercial and non-single-family properties, would be included.

budget_items.topic: Minimum square footage threshold for GIS parcel review
budget_items.what_was_said: The minimum square footage a property must have to be looked at was raised from the original Concord-based proposal figure to a higher figure in the new proposal.

The task force discussed removing most of the fee-structure work since they feel comfortable with what was already proposed for the town's own tiers, leaving Weston and Sampson to do a smaller review/advisory pass.

budget_items.topic: Task 2 cost - fee structure review, town vs. Concord comparison
budget_items.what_was_said: The cost for this task was compared to what Weston and Sampson charged Concord for similar work, and the new town figure was read out.
This task's cost was reported to have stayed the same as the prior proposal; printing and distribution costs are not included in the scope.

budget_items.topic: Meetings and project management scope and cost
budget_items.what_was_said: The number of small-group, public, and monthly progress meetings was cut roughly in half to a third, and the associated cost was reduced.

budget_items.topic: Total revised Weston and Sampson proposal cost
budget_items.what_was_said: The task force said the overall proposal cost was brought down substantially from the original figure after asking the consultant what budget they were targeting.

budget_items.topic: Task force's own budget vs. proposal cost
budget_items.what_was_said: A member said their current budget does not cover the new proposal cost and described a worst-case shortfall, noting the town manager has it covered but more money is still needed.

budget_items.topic: Reappropriation of old, unspent capital project funds
budget_items.what_was_said: Funding for the stormwater work is proposed to come from previously allocated but unspent capital project money, to be reappropriated via a town meeting warrant article.

decisions.decision: Task force confirmed removal of the background data collection task (Task 1) from the Weston and Sampson scope, per their prior meeting direction.
Task force confirmed removal of the ArcGIS online web application/tool (Task 5) from the scope.
Task force kept a placeholder on the November town meeting warrant to give an update on the stormwater utility work, aiming for a spring decision timeline.
Task force agreed to try to meet the first week of December, after town meeting and Thanksgiving.

minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Stormwater Task Force reviewed a revised, scaled-back proposal from consultant Weston and Sampson for a stormwater utility feasibility study, after members had met with the firm to cut scope items including background data collection, a DPW capabilities assessment, and an ArcGIS online tool, in order to roughly halve the cost. The task force voted to approve the revised proposal dated October 10, 2025, discussed funding it via reappropriation of unspent old capital project money through a November town meeting warrant article, and received an update that earthwork on their demonstration BMP project is complete with a kiosk and drainage grates still to be installed.

what_happened.line: Task force voted to approve a scaled-back proposal from Weston and Sampson for a stormwater utility feasibility study.
Funding is proposed to come from reappropriating unspent money from an older capital project, via a November town meeting warrant article.
A member said the task force's current budget does not cover the revised proposal cost, though the town manager said it is covered.
Earthwork on the task force's demonstration stormwater project is complete; a kiosk and drainage grates remain to be installed.

why_it_matters: This feeds a November town meeting warrant article asking voters to reappropriate old, unspent capital funds rather than raise new money.
The study is a step toward a possible future stormwater utility fee, which could become a new charge on property owners if the town creates one.
